Where is Las Vegas and how is the city laid out?

Las Vegas sits in a basin on the floor of the Mojave Desert, ringed by mountain ranges, at about 2,000 feet above sea level. The city covers roughly 142 square miles on its own, while the wider urban area runs to about 540 square miles.

That size matters when you sell a house here. A house in Centennial Hills and one near Downtown can both carry a Las Vegas address while being very different properties.

Wikipedia's list of city neighborhoods includes Angel Park, Canyon Gate, Centennial Hills, Charleston, Desert Shores, Downtown, East Las Vegas, The Lakes, La Madre Foothills, Lone Mountain, Peccole Ranch, Queensridge, Rancho, Summerlin, Tule Springs, Twin Lakes and West Las Vegas. Each has its own mix of build years, lot sizes and homeowners associations, which shapes what repairs a buyer will expect to see.

What is the history of Las Vegas in brief?

Las Vegas was founded on May 15, 1905, when 110 acres next to the Union Pacific Railroad tracks were auctioned off. The city was incorporated on March 16, 1911.

Houses built in different decades differ in roofing, windows, air conditioning and wiring, and those differences drive the repair lists that make a traditional listing expensive.

How does the Las Vegas economy affect a house sale?

Tourism, gaming and conventions are the primary drivers of the Las Vegas economy, according to the city's general reference entry, with employers such as Zappos.com, Allegiant Air and Planet 13 Holdings also named.

For a seller, an economy built on hospitality means that income can shift with visitor traffic and shift schedules. Owners who lose hours, relocate for work or inherit a house from a relative who worked on the Strip often need to sell on a timeline set by someone else. A cash sale suits that situation because the closing date is something you and the buyer agree on, not something a lender sets for you.

  • Job changes and relocation are common reasons for a quick sale.
  • Inherited houses often arrive with deferred maintenance and a pile of paperwork.
  • Landlords with tenants in place sometimes prefer a buyer who takes the property as it stands.

What does desert heat and flash flooding mean for a Las Vegas house?

Las Vegas has a hot desert climate, with July the hottest month at an average daytime high of 104.5 degrees Fahrenheit and only about 4.2 inches of rain a year spread over roughly 26 rainy days.

The heat is hard on air conditioning systems, roof membranes, stucco, irrigation lines and pool equipment. An inspector will look at the age of the AC unit first. If it is near the end of its life, a buyer using a loan will usually ask for a repair credit or a replacement, which is one more reason sellers with older systems consider selling as-is.

Rain is rare but can arrive hard. The Clark County Regional Flood Control District was set up in 1986 after a series of flooding events in the valley in the 1970s and early 1980s. Clark County also warns that homeowner's insurance policies do not cover flood damage and points owners to the National Flood Insurance Program. If a buyer's lender requires flood coverage on your parcel, that can surface late in the process.

Which roads and airports matter to Las Vegas sellers?

Interstate 15, Interstate 11, Interstate 215, US 95, the Summerlin Parkway and the 215 beltway are the main arteries in Las Vegas, and Harry Reid International Airport serves the valley.

Drive times to those corridors are what buyers ask about first, so a short line in your sale paperwork about proximity to the freeway or the beltway helps. Noise near a major road is something buyers notice on a first visit, so mention it up front.

Which school district serves Las Vegas?

The Clark County School District serves Las Vegas. The district describes itself as the nation's fifth-largest, and its police services page cites more than 296,000 students across 374 schools.

Because attendance zones in a district this large change over time, the district's open enrollment program lets families apply to up to five schools or programs. If a buyer asks which school a house is zoned for, point them to the district rather than quoting a name from memory.

What disclosures and taxes apply when you sell a house in Las Vegas?

Nevada law requires a seller of residential property to complete the Real Estate Division's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form, listing known conditions that materially affect the property. The statute is NRS 113.130, and the form is Form 547.

The state's residential guide notes that a buyer who closes without a completed form, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless the buyer waives that right under NRS 113.150(6). That is a serious consequence, so answer the form honestly and in full.

The other cost tied to the deed is the real property transfer tax. The state page lists $1.95 for every $500 of value, with an extra $0.60 in Clark County, which brings the statutory rate to $2.55 per $500. Each deed presented to the county recorder must be accompanied by a declaration of value, and NRS 375 says the tax can be collected from either the buyer or the seller, so the contract should say who pays it.

Can a Las Vegas house keep operating as a short-term rental after a sale?

Not automatically, because the city sets eligibility rules for each new license. The City of Las Vegas defines a short-term residential rental as a house or condominium rented to guests for fewer than 31 consecutive days.

For a new license, the city's 2026 instructions say the residence must be at least 660 feet from any other short-term residential rental and 2,500 feet from a resort hotel, sit in a zone that allows the use, and have written HOA permission where an association exists. If you are selling a house that has been used as a rental, ask the Business Licensing Division what happens to the license at transfer, and tell buyers plainly what you know.

How do Clark County property taxes work when you sell?

Property taxes in Las Vegas are billed by Clark County and due on the third Monday in August, though owners can pay in installments when the taxes on a parcel exceed $100.

The Treasurer lists the installment dates as the third Monday in August, then the first Mondays of October, January and March. The Treasurer mails real property tax bills only once each fiscal year, and owners who have not received one by August 1 can request a copy through the automated phone system. Late payments carry penalties under NRS 361.483, starting at 4 percent on a late installment.

If you disagree with your assessment, an appeal to the County Board of Equalization must be filed on or before January 15. Owner-occupants also have a partial abatement under NRS 361.4723 that keeps a primary residence's tax increase near 3 percent a year, and the statute excludes homes rented to others.

What does a cash sale look like in Las Vegas?

A cash sale means the buyer is not relying on a mortgage, so there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait on.

The usual steps are an offer, a title search, the seller's disclosure form, a signed contract, a closing with a title or escrow company, a deed and a declaration of value presented for recording. Your own timeline depends on the condition of title, any liens, whether tenants occupy the house and how quickly the HOA, if there is one, answers requests for documents.

Cash Home Buyers does not promise a specific price. We look at the house as it is, and you can decline an offer without owing anything.

What do Las Vegas sellers usually face?

These situations often make a conventional listing hard.

  • An aging air conditioning system, roof or pool that would draw repair requests.
  • An inherited house that needs probate or a transfer on death deed to be completed first.
  • A tenant in place, or a rental with an unclear short-term license.
  • HOA documents, assessments or violations that must be sorted before closing.
  • A loan balance, tax installment or other lien that needs to be paid at closing.

Each of these can be handled in a cash sale, though the order of operations varies. Gather your deed, the latest tax bill, any HOA statements and the mortgage payoff before you talk to a buyer, and the process moves faster.

More questions about Las Vegas, NV

How much is the transfer tax when I sell a house in Las Vegas?

The statutory rate in Clark County is $2.55 for every $500 of value, made up of the $1.95 state rate plus a $0.60 Clark County add-on. NRS 375 allows collection from either the buyer or the seller, so the purchase contract decides who pays.

Do I have to fill out a seller disclosure in Nevada?

Yes, a seller of residential property must complete the Real Estate Division's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form under NRS 113.130. A buyer who closes without it, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless that right was waived.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

Taxes are due on the third Monday in August, and parcels with taxes over $100 can be paid in four installments. The other installments fall on the first Monday of October, January and March.

How long do I have to appeal my Las Vegas property assessment?

An appeal to the Clark County Board of Equalization must be filed on or before January 15. If January 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.

Does the turf removal law force me to tear out my grass before selling?

No, not for a single-family home. The Southern Nevada Water Authority says the law, which bars using Colorado River water on nonfunctional grass from 2027, applies to commercial, multi-family, government and other properties and does not apply to grass in single-family yards.

Where is Henderson, Nevada?

Henderson is a city in Clark County about 16 miles southeast of Las Vegas, at an elevation of roughly 1,867 feet. It covers about 107 square miles, almost all of it land.

The Census Bureau estimates 353,289 residents as of July 1, 2025, and Wikipedia ranks Henderson second in population in Nevada, after Las Vegas. It is part of the Las Vegas Valley metropolitan area, which means a Henderson seller shares a market, an airport and a school district with its larger neighbor while dealing with a different city hall.

How did Henderson grow from a wartime plant to a master-planned city?

Henderson was incorporated on April 16, 1953, and was first known for magnesium production during World War II at the Basic Magnesium plant.

Growth since then has come largely through master-planned communities, beginning with Green Valley. Wikipedia lists Green Valley, Anthem, Lake Las Vegas and Seven Hills among them, and notes that the city also redeveloped and reinvested after the PEPCON disaster. Many master-planned neighborhoods have homeowners associations, so check early whether yours does.

  • Green Valley, the first large master-planned neighborhood.
  • Anthem, Seven Hills and Lake Las Vegas, later communities with their own rules.
  • Older parts of the city, where you should confirm whether any association applies.

What do Henderson's employers mean for a home sale?

Henderson's economy covers logistics, electrical equipment manufacturing, financial and credit services, media and sports production, and back-office support, according to Wikipedia's summary of the city.

The employers it lists include the City of Henderson, Barclays Services, Green Valley Ranch Resort, St. Rose Dominican Hospital, Henderson Hospital, an Amazon distribution center, Sunset Station, the M Resort and the Las Vegas Raiders. Owners whose jobs move or end sometimes need to sell on a short timeline.

How does the Henderson climate affect a house?

Henderson has a hot desert climate with mild winters and hot summers, which puts the most strain on roofs, cooling equipment, exterior paint and landscaping.

The Las Vegas Valley also sees flash flooding when storms arrive. Clark County states that homeowner's insurance does not cover flood damage and recommends the National Flood Insurance Program, and the Clark County Regional Flood Control District, created in 1986, manages drainage across the valley. Ask your insurance agent whether your parcel is in a mapped flood zone before a buyer's lender does.

A seller with an old air conditioner or a leaking roof should expect a buyer using a mortgage to ask for repairs. Buyers who pay cash can accept the house with those items unresolved and adjust the offer accordingly.

Which roads connect Henderson to the rest of the valley?

Interstate 11, Interstate 215, Boulder Highway (State Route 582), Lake Mead Parkway (State Route 564) and St. Rose Parkway (State Route 146) are Henderson's main routes.

Henderson also has over 220 miles of trails and 72 parks, according to Wikipedia. Proximity to a trail, park or freeway entrance is something you can state accurately in your paperwork, and buyers weigh it alongside commute time to the Strip, the airport and the hospitals.

What school district serves Henderson?

The Clark County School District serves Henderson, the same district that covers Las Vegas.

The district reports more than 296,000 students across 374 schools, and its open enrollment page says families can apply to up to five schools or programs. Zoning for a particular address should come from the district, not from a seller's memory.

Can I run a short-term rental in Henderson, and what happens when I sell?

Henderson allows short-term vacation rentals only with annual city registration, and some developments are on a prohibited list where the city will not register a property.

The city's page lists a non-refundable registration fee of $848, a short-term rental certification class for the owner and the local contact, a Nevada business license in the owner's name, and a registered local contact who is either certified or a licensed property manager under NRS 645. Registered properties must also file the room tax report and pay transient lodging tax monthly. Henderson's acknowledgement form further requires that the rental be expressly authorized by the association if the home sits in a common-interest community.

If you own a house that has been rented to visitors, tell buyers whether the registration is current. Do not assume a registration carries over to a new owner without checking with the city.

What does Henderson's turf law mean for a seller?

Nevada's 2021 law on nonfunctional turf does not apply to grass in single-family yards.

The Southern Nevada Water Authority says the law bars the use of Colorado River water delivered by member agencies on nonfunctional grass starting in 2027, and that it applies to commercial, multi-family, government and other properties. If your Henderson home is a condominium or sits in an association with common-area grass, the association is the party that faces the deadline, and its budget may include a special assessment that a buyer will ask about.

What disclosures and taxes apply to a Henderson sale?

A Henderson seller must complete Nevada's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form, and the statutory transfer tax in Clark County is $2.55 per $500 of value.

The form is required by NRS 113.130. Nevada's residential guide warns that a buyer who closes without a completed form, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless the buyer waives that right.

The tax is the state's $1.95 per $500 plus a $0.60 Clark County add-on. The deed goes to the county recorder with a declaration of value, and NRS 375 says the tax can be collected from the buyer or the seller, so check who pays in your contract.

How are Henderson property taxes billed and appealed?

Clark County bills property tax for Henderson parcels, and the taxes are due on the third Monday in August, with installments available on parcels over $100.

The remaining installments fall on the first Mondays of October, January and March. NRS 361.483 adds a 4 percent penalty to one late installment, rising with each additional missed installment. To contest an assessed value, file with the County Board of Equalization on or before January 15 of the fiscal year, or the next business day when January 15 falls on a weekend or holiday.

For a primary residence, NRS 361.4723 limits the annual increase in the tax bill to about 3 percent, but the statute defines a primary residence as one not rented to anyone besides the owner and family. A house that has been a rental may therefore not qualify.

How does a cash sale work in Henderson?

In a cash sale the buyer pays without a mortgage, so the closing does not wait on a lender appraisal.

You still deliver the disclosure form, clear title, settle any HOA balance, pay off a mortgage or lien at closing and sign the deed. Cash Home Buyers reviews the house as it stands and does not promise a figure in advance. If you decide the offer is not right, you owe nothing.

  • Collect your deed, loan payoff statement and latest tax bill.
  • Request a current HOA statement and the governing documents.
  • List any repairs you know about so the disclosure form is complete.

More questions about Henderson, NV

How far is Henderson from Las Vegas?

Henderson is about 16 miles southeast of Las Vegas. Both are in Clark County and share the Clark County School District.

How much does a Henderson short-term rental registration cost?

The City of Henderson lists a non-refundable annual registration fee of $848 per property. Owners also need a Nevada business license, a certification class and a qualifying local contact.

Is there a transfer tax when I sell in Henderson?

Yes, the statutory rate in Clark County is $2.55 per $500 of value. The contract decides whether the buyer or the seller pays, since NRS 375 allows either.

Do I need to remove my front lawn before selling?

No. The Southern Nevada Water Authority states that the nonfunctional turf law does not apply to grass in single-family homes, including front and back yards.

When can I appeal my Henderson property tax assessment?

Appeals go to the Clark County Board of Equalization and must be filed on or before January 15. When that date lands on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.

Cash Home Buyers in Nevada

  • North Las Vegas, NV: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a North Las Vegas, NV sale

Sell Your North Las Vegas House for Cash

Tell us about your North Las Vegas house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

North Las Vegas at a glance

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 296,653 (Census Bureau).
Selling in North Las Vegas?
We buy North Las Vegas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is North Las Vegas and how did it become a city?

North Las Vegas is a suburban city in Clark County that sits northeast of Las Vegas in the Mojave Desert. It covers about 101 square miles and is the fourth most populous city in Nevada.

The town began in 1919, when Thomas L. Williams moved his family onto a 160-acre piece of land about a mile from Las Vegas and started building wells, roads and irrigation ditches. Workers from the Hoover Dam project settled there between 1928 and 1935. The city was incorporated on May 1, 1946. Locals still use the nicknames Old Town and North Town.

Newer parts of the city include the master-planned communities of Aliante and Eldorado, so a house here can be anything from an older lot near the original townsite to a recent subdivision home.

What are the basic facts about North Las Vegas?

The table below pulls together the figures a seller is most likely to be asked about. Population history comes from the decennial census, with the 2025 figure being the Census Bureau estimate.

Growth is the main story. The city roughly doubled between 2000 and 2010, then kept adding residents through 2020.

What does the desert climate mean for a North Las Vegas house?

North Las Vegas has a desert climate, so heat is the main stress on a house here. Mean daily highs reach about 105 degrees in July, and the record high is 119 degrees. Average yearly precipitation is only about 4.6 inches.

Winters are mild during the day, but nights often fall below freezing, and snow shows up only once every few years. In summer, monsoon storms can bring heavy rain and thunderstorms.

Worth checking before you list or ask for an offer:

  • The age and condition of the air conditioning system, since it runs for most of the year
  • Roof membranes and tile, which take direct sun for months
  • Block walls and fences, which the city lists as a code enforcement concern when they are damaged

You do not have to repair any of this to sell for cash, but you do have to disclose what you know.

Who employs people in North Las Vegas?

The local economy leans on warehousing, distribution and manufacturing. Amazon opened an 850,000-square-foot fulfillment center in the city on May 12, 2019, and it employs more than 1,500 people. Sephora opened a 715,000-square-foot distribution center in October 2019.

Bigelow Aerospace is headquartered in North Las Vegas, and the Apex Industrial Park is now part of the city. In June 2024, PCM Railone AG announced a production facility for concrete ties and a North American headquarters in the city, tied to the Brightline West high-speed rail project. The Clark County School District is also a major employer across the county.

Which schools, roads and services serve North Las Vegas homes?

Public schools are run by the Clark County School District, which the Wikipedia article on the city describes as the fifth largest in the country. High schools inside North Las Vegas include Canyon Springs, Cheyenne, Legacy, Mojave and Rancho. The Cheyenne Campus of the College of Southern Nevada is also in the city.

The city itself provides police and fire protection, parks and recreation, and water and wastewater service. It maintains 34 parks on more than 475 acres of developed park land. RTC Transit runs buses across the Las Vegas area, and North Las Vegas Airport, established on December 7, 1941, handles tour flights.

What city rules can slow a North Las Vegas sale?

Open code enforcement problems and short-term rental permits are the two local rules that most often complicate a sale. Both are handled at the city level, not by Clark County.

The Code Enforcement Division says it focuses on the following problems:

  • Boarding and securing vacant structures
  • Junk, litter, garbage and overgrown weeds
  • Junk vehicles and illegally posted signs
  • Illegal home businesses
  • Obstructed streets or sidewalks and damaged fences or block walls

The division aims for voluntary compliance through notices and education, and it can abate nuisances or issue criminal citations when that fails. The city has an appeal and hearing process. Clear any open case before closing or tell the buyer about it.

Short-term rentals need more. The city adopted Ordinance 3127 in June 2022, and an owner must win a Conditional Use Permit before applying for a business license. The application requires a notarized letter from the homeowners association, a 660-foot separation from other short-term rentals and a 2,500-foot separation from resort hotels. Planning and Zoning answers questions at (702) 633-1537.

What does Nevada require when you sell a house in North Las Vegas?

Nevada requires the seller to complete a disclosure form at least 10 days before the property is conveyed, and that duty applies to a cash sale as well. Under NRS 113.130, the seller completes the form and the seller or the agent serves it on the buyer or the buyer's agent. An agent may not fill it out for you. If you later find a new defect, or learn that a listed defect got worse, you must tell the buyer in writing before closing.

The statute lists exceptions, including sales by foreclosure, sales between co-owners, spouses or close relatives, the first sale of a house built by a licensed contractor, and certain sales by fiduciaries such as a personal representative or trustee. A buyer cannot waive the requirement.

Real property transfer tax is the other fixed cost. In Clark County the rate is $2.55 per $500 of value, which is the statewide $1.95 plus a $0.60 Clark County add-on, according to the Nevada Department of Taxation. On a sale at $400,000, that works out to $2,040. The tax is collected by the County Recorder when the deed is recorded, and the state says the buyer and the seller are responsible together and individually. Who actually pays is a matter for the purchase contract. Exemptions under NRS 375.090 include a transfer between former spouses under a divorce decree and a deed that takes effect on death.

If the house is in a homeowners association, the owner must furnish a resale package under NRS 116.4109. It includes the governing documents, a statement of unpaid assessments and fines, and the budget. The buyer can cancel until midnight of the fifth calendar day after receiving it.

How are property taxes handled when a North Las Vegas house sells?

The Clark County Treasurer bills real property tax once a year, and taxes are due the third Monday in August. If the bill is more than $100, you may pay in four installments. Those are the third Monday in August, and the first Mondays in October, January and March. The payments are not quarterly.

Payment must arrive within 10 days of the due date to avoid a penalty. For one late installment the penalty is 4 percent of the installment. Unpaid taxes at the end of April are advertised as delinquent, and if the amount is still owed on the first Monday in June, the county holds the property for a two-year redemption period, with interest at 10 percent a year.

If you are behind, ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure early. The office is at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, phone (702) 455-4323, open Monday through Thursday.

How does a cash sale of a North Las Vegas house work?

A cash sale replaces the lender with the buyer's own funds, which removes the loan approval and most of the appraisal delay. Everything else on the Nevada side still applies: the disclosure form, the recorded deed, the transfer tax and any association paperwork.

Typical steps run in this order:

  • You send the address and condition of the house and receive a written offer
  • A title company opens escrow and searches for liens, unpaid taxes and judgments
  • You complete the Nevada seller's disclosure and any HOA package
  • The deed is signed and recorded with the Clark County Recorder, with a Declaration of Value
  • Payoffs and fees are paid from proceeds and you receive the balance

We buy North Las Vegas houses as-is. We cannot promise a price before we see the property, and you are free to compare our written offer with a listing.

More questions about North Las Vegas, NV

Do I have to disclose problems if I sell my North Las Vegas house for cash?

Yes. NRS 113.130 requires the seller to complete a disclosure form at least 10 days before the property is conveyed, and the exceptions do not include cash sales. You only have to disclose defects you know about, and you must update the buyer in writing if you learn of a new one before closing.

How much is the transfer tax on a North Las Vegas sale?

In Clark County the rate is $2.55 per $500 of value, which is $1.95 statewide plus $0.60 for Clark County. A $400,000 sale would carry $2,040 of tax. The County Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded, and the contract decides who pays.

Can a North Las Vegas buyer turn my house into a short-term rental?

Only with a Conditional Use Permit from the city, which must come before a business license. The application needs a 660-foot separation from other short-term rentals, a 2,500-foot separation from resort hotels and a notarized letter from the HOA where one applies.

What happens if code enforcement has an open case on my house?

Code Enforcement can abate a nuisance or issue citations when notices are ignored. You can appeal through the city. Resolve the case before closing where you can, and tell the buyer about anything still open.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

Taxes are due the third Monday in August. If the bill exceeds $100 you can pay in installments on the third Monday in August and the first Mondays in October, January and March. Late payments carry penalties, starting at 4 percent for one late installment.

Does my HOA have to give the buyer documents when I sell?

Yes. NRS 116.4109 requires a resale package with the governing documents, a statement of what you owe, the budget and pending legal actions. The buyer may cancel within five calendar days of receiving it, and the association must respond to your written request within 10 calendar days.

Where is Reno and what is it known for?

Reno is the county seat and largest city of Washoe County, in northwest Nevada along the California border. It sits in the Truckee River valley on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada, about 23 miles northeast of Lake Tahoe, at an elevation near 4,400 feet.

The city is named for Union Major General Jesse L. Reno. For much of the twentieth century it drew people who came for Nevada's divorce laws, and it was the state's largest city until the 1960 census showed Las Vegas ahead. Today it is the home of the University of Nevada, Reno, and a gaming and tourism center. The 2020 census counted 264,165 residents.

Downtown Reno and Sparks share a valley called the Truckee Meadows. The Reno-Sparks metro area covers Washoe, Lyon and Storey counties.

What does Reno's weather mean for a house?

Reno has a cold semi-arid climate with moderately cold winters and hot summers, so a house here deals with freezing temperatures, wind and dry heat in the same year. The temperature reaches or falls below freezing on 122 days a year, and there are about 65 days with highs of 90 degrees or more. The record low is minus 17 degrees and the record high is 108 degrees.

Most precipitation comes in fall, winter and spring. Western parts of the city can get three to four times as much as areas to the east. Summer thunderstorms can occur from April to October, and the region is windy throughout the year.

  • Freeze and thaw cycles put stress on pipes, hose bibs and exterior paint
  • Wind and temperature swings wear roofing and fencing
  • Western neighborhoods see much more precipitation than eastern ones

A seller who has put off maintenance on any of these is not obliged to fix it before a cash sale, but known defects go on the Nevada disclosure form.

How much wildfire and earthquake risk does Reno have?

Wildfire is the most serious hazard for Reno houses, particularly on the southwest side. Roughly 80 percent of homes in the area carry some risk of being affected by a wildfire.

Wikipedia's Washoe County article also calls the county wildfire prone, with the risk concentrated in southern Reno and just outside the city limits. If your house is near a forested edge, say so on the disclosure form.

Who are the biggest employers in Reno?

Education, health care and casinos lead the list. According to Reno's 2025 annual financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, the city's top employers are as follows.

  • Washoe County School District, about 7,500 employees
  • Renown Regional Medical Center, about 7,500
  • Peppermill Reno, Grand Sierra Resort, Saint Mary's Regional Medical Center, Eldorado Resort Casino, Silver Legacy, University of Nevada, Reno, U-Haul Holding Company and Circus Circus Reno, about 3,000 each

Outside the city limits, the Tesla Gigafactory at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center employs roughly 11,000 people, which is more than any single employer in Reno. Data centers at the same industrial center and at Reno Technology Park, along with distribution facilities for Amazon, Walmart and PetSmart, have widened the region's economy beyond gaming. Ormat Technologies, a geothermal company, is headquartered in Reno.

How do roads, transit and schools serve Reno homes?

Interstate 80 runs through downtown Reno, and US 395 and Interstate 580 are the main north-south route. The Regional Transportation Commission of Washoe County runs the bus system, with its main terminal on 4th Street downtown. Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at Reno station, and Reno-Tahoe International Airport is the second busiest commercial airport in Nevada.

The Washoe County School District serves the whole county. The University of Nevada, Reno, founded as a state college in 1886 and now enrolling about 21,000 students, anchors the north side of downtown. Truckee Meadows Community College has about 13,000 students.

What city rules can affect a Reno sale?

The City of Reno enforces property maintenance through its Code Enforcement department, and an unresolved violation can be recorded against your house. The Reno Municipal Code covers things such as inoperable vehicles, trash and debris, overgrown landscaping, work done without permits and zoning violations.

The process goes in steps:

  • A warning of violation letter gives a compliance date, generally about 30 days
  • If the problem remains, an administrative citation follows: $100 for the first, $250 for the second, $500 for the third on residential property
  • A notice of intent to record can lead to a recorded notice of violation lien with the Washoe County Recorder
  • The lien is released only after the problem is fixed and all fines and fees are paid

Owners may appeal through the City Clerk's office, and the city says code officers cannot waive or reduce fines. Complaints and questions go to Reno Direct at 775-334-4636. Other rules sellers run into: vehicles cannot be parked in the front yard, inoperable vehicles must be screened, and items such as couches, mattresses and appliances cannot be stored in view in a front or side yard. Clear these before photos or a walkthrough, and check whether a lien is already recorded.

The city adopted its 2024 building codes on July 1, 2025. If you are finishing unpermitted work before a sale, ask Building about permit status first.

What does Nevada require from a Reno seller?

A Reno seller must complete the state disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance, and the rule does not exempt cash sales. NRS 113.130 says the seller, not the agent, completes it, and that the buyer cannot waive it. Exceptions include foreclosure sales, sales between spouses or close relatives, and certain sales by fiduciaries such as trustees and personal representatives.

Washoe County adds $0.10 to the statewide real property transfer tax rate, so the rate is $2.05 per $500 of value. On a $450,000 sale that is $1,845. The Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded. A Declaration of Value form must accompany any document that transfers title. The basis is the sale price or the estimated fair market value, which comes from the assessor's taxable value or a prior purchase price within the last five years, whichever is higher. The Property Transfer Compliance Recorder takes questions at (775) 328-3661. Under state guidance both buyer and seller are liable for the tax, so your contract should say who pays.

Homeowners association sales require the resale package described in NRS 116.4109, and the buyer has five calendar days after receiving it to cancel.

How does Washoe County property tax work for a Reno seller?

The Washoe County Treasurer bills property tax. Bills go out by August 1, and the 2026-27 installments fall on August 17, October 5, January 4 and March 1. A parcel with more than $100 of tax can pay in four installments. Delinquent property is advertised and owners have two years from the lien filing to redeem it.

The Assessor handles values and a tax cap. Nevada's 2005 law, Assembly Bill 489, caps the increase in the tax bill, not the assessed value, at 3 percent on a primary residence, with a higher cap on other property. After a change of ownership the Assessor mails an affidavit, and until a qualifying one is filed the status stays at the higher cap. That is a point to raise with a buyer. Appeals of value go to the County Board of Equalization by January 15.

How does selling a Reno house for cash work?

A cash purchase skips lender underwriting, so the timeline is driven by title work and the recording step at the Washoe County Recorder. You can ask for an offer with only the address and a description of condition, and we do not charge fees or commissions. If you decline the offer you owe nothing.

Expect to provide the disclosure form, clear any recorded code liens, and confirm the tax status. We buy Reno houses as-is, including houses with deferred maintenance, tenants or probate issues.

Is Reno at risk of wildfire?

Yes. Wikipedia's Reno article says roughly 80 percent of homes in the area have some risk, and the Davis Fire in September 2024 burned 14 structures and led to about 20,000 evacuations. Southwest Reno carries the most risk.

What is the transfer tax on a Reno home sale?

Washoe County's rate is $2.05 per $500 of value, which is the $1.95 statewide rate plus $0.10. A $450,000 sale carries $1,845. The County Recorder collects it at recording, and the buyer and seller are both liable under state guidance.

Can Reno code enforcement put a lien on my house?

Yes. After warnings and citations, the city can record a notice of violation lien with the Washoe County Recorder. It is released only after the violation is fixed and all fines and fees are paid. Residential citations are $100, $250 and $500 on the escalating scale.

Do I have to make repairs before a cash sale in Reno?

No repair is required by the sale itself. You must disclose known defects on the Nevada seller's disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance, and open code violations or unpermitted work are worth raising with the buyer.

When is the Washoe County appeal deadline?

Appeals to the County Board of Equalization must be filed by January 15, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or holiday. A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Equalization by March 10.

Does the Nevada disclosure rule apply to cash sales?

Yes. NRS 113.130 applies to residential property whatever the financing, with specific exceptions such as foreclosure sales and sales between close relatives.

Where is Sparks and how did it start?

In 1904 the Southern Pacific Railroad built a switch yard and maintenance sheds there after moving its division point from Wadsworth. The company gave its employees a 50-by-140-foot lot for $1 and offered to move houses from Wadsworth for free. The town was first called Harriman and then renamed for John Sparks, who was governor of Nevada from 1903 to 1908. Its nickname is the Rail City.

Sparks stayed small until the 1950s, when growth in Reno set off a housing boom north of the tracks. In the 1970s the area south of the railroad filled with warehouses and light industry.

Washoe County, not the city, bills and collects the property tax on Sparks houses. The county's fiscal year runs from July 1 through June 30, and July 1 is the lien date. The Treasurer mails bills by August 1, and for 2026-27 the installments are due August 17, October 5, January 4 and March 1.

Carson City was founded in 1858 after Abraham Curry bought Eagle Station, and it was incorporated in 1875.

Where is Fernley, Nevada?

Fernley is a city in Lyon County, in the Reno-Tahoe-Sparks metropolitan area, at the junction of Interstate 80, US Alternate 50 and US Alternate 95.

Its elevation is about 4,636 feet, and its total area is 128.39 square miles, of which 121.65 is land. The Census Bureau estimates 26,214 residents as of July 1, 2025. The Reno-Tahoe-Sparks grouping means Fernley sellers often compare their house with others in the wider Reno area, though the city has its own character and its own flood history.

How did Fernley begin, and when did it become a city?

Fernley was established in 1904 as an agricultural and ranching community, and it incorporated as a city on July 1, 2001.

Its farmland came from the Newlands Irrigation Project, which followed the Newlands Reclamation Act of 1902. The Southern Pacific Railroad completed the Fernley and Lassen Railway in 1914. Industry arrived later: the Nevada Cement Company opened in 1965 and began the shift toward an industrial and commuter base.

What happened in the 2008 Fernley flood?

On January 5, 2008, the north embankment of the Truckee Canal breached inside Fernley after a winter storm, flooding approximately 590 homes, according to the Truckee-Carson Irrigation District.

Wikipedia reports that about 3,500 people were evacuated and that 3 to 6 feet of water filled houses. A dam safety review says water flowed through the breach for up to 9 hours and reached depths up to 8 feet in places. Repairs were made in February 2008 and the canal reopened in March 2008. A federal class action over the flooding settled for nearly $18.2 million, according to Courthouse News.

The canal conveys water to approximately 3,000 water right holders, including individual landowners, farmers and the City of Fernley. Since 2008 its flows have been reduced and it has been run under water-level limits, and the later lining project allows flows above 500 cubic feet per second.

The canal itself was addressed later. The irrigation district's Public Safety Project involved 3.56 miles of full-prism lining, replacement of the Fernley Check Structure and other work. The district received a record of decision in December 2020, began work in November 2022 and declared the project substantially complete in July 2024.

Does that flood history affect selling a Fernley house?

It can, because a buyer or lender may ask whether the house sits in a flood zone or has had water damage.

Nevada's disclosure form requires a seller to state known conditions that materially affect the property, and a house that took on water in 2008 should be described honestly, including repairs and any claims. Check with the City of Fernley or your insurance agent about flood zone status for your parcel, and note that Clark County, in a separate statement, points out that standard homeowner's policies do not cover flood damage. If you are not sure whether your policy includes it, read it before you list.

  • Gather repair records and permits if the house was repaired after the flood.
  • Ask your insurer what your policy covers.
  • Tell buyers what you know. Nevada law allows treble damages when a known defect goes undisclosed.

What does the Fernley economy look like?

Transport, storage and distribution are Fernley's largest industry employers, according to the City of Fernley's employer page.

Wikipedia lists an Amazon order fulfillment center of 750,000 square feet that opened in 1999, plus Trex, UPS Worldwide Logistics, Johns Manville, Sherwin Williams and Polaris in the industrial park. The Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, about 15 miles west, is home to Tesla's Gigafactory. The US Department of Transportation says the Victory Infrastructure Project will connect Interstate 80 to Highway 50 and serve the Victory Logistics District, which it expects to create 7,000 to 10,000 jobs over five years. That is a projection, not a count.

Owners who lose a job, transfer or change employers sometimes need to sell on a short timeline.

What is the Fernley climate like for a house?

Fernley has a cold desert climate with an average of about 5 inches of rain a year, cold winters with some snow and hot, very dry summers.

Sun and dryness wear on roofing, fences and exterior paint, and winter cold can stress pipes and heating equipment. Buyers who use a loan will see these items in the inspection report and may ask for repairs. Buyers who pay cash can take the house as it stands.

Which school district and roads serve Fernley?

The Lyon County School District serves Fernley, with Fernley High School, Fernley Intermediate School and the Fernley Adult Education Center among its local sites.

Interstate 80, US Alternate 50 and US Alternate 95 are the main roads. Buyers commuting to Reno, Sparks or the industrial park will want to know your address's drive time to the interstate.

What disclosures and transfer tax apply to a Fernley sale?

A Fernley seller must complete Nevada's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form under NRS 113.130, and the transfer tax is $1.95 per $500 of value, the base state rate.

The state page lists the base rate for all counties and names only Washoe, Churchill and Clark as having extra amounts, so Lyon County sits on the base rate. Confirm the amount with your title company. The deed must be presented to the county recorder with a declaration of value, and NRS 375 says the tax may be collected from the buyer or the seller, so the contract should name the payer.

How are Lyon County property taxes billed?

Lyon County bills Fernley property taxes on the Nevada schedule: the third Monday of August, then the first Mondays of October, January and March.

Lyon County's website confirms those four installment dates, and NRS 361.483 sets penalties that start at 4 percent for one late installment. The statute allows installments only when the taxes on the parcel exceed $100. Owners of a single-family primary residence can claim the partial abatement in NRS 361.4723, which keeps the yearly increase near 3 percent, but a house rented to others does not qualify.

More questions about Fernley, NV

What caused the 2008 Fernley flood?

A levee on the north side of the Truckee Canal breached on January 5, 2008 after a winter storm. The irrigation district says approximately 590 homes were flooded.

Was the Truckee Canal repaired?

Yes. Emergency repairs were made in 2008, and the irrigation district's Public Safety Project, including 3.56 miles of full-prism lining, was declared substantially complete in July 2024.

How much is the transfer tax when selling in Fernley?

The state's base rate is $1.95 per $500 of value, and the page names add-ons only for Washoe, Churchill and Clark counties. Lyon County is not among them, but confirm with your title company.

When are Lyon County property taxes due?

They are due the third Monday of August, with installments on the first Mondays of October, January and March. Installments are available when taxes exceed $100.

Which school district is Fernley in?

Fernley is in the Lyon County School District, which includes Fernley High School and Fernley Intermediate School.
